results.claim: The six advertised block cardinalities sum to 76.
results.proof_sketch: Exact integer arithmetic gives 6+18+16+14+16+6=76. This establishes only the numerical sum of the advertised block cardinalities; it does not by itself instantiate the source-model tuple A=(Cl,Init,T).

results.claim: For any fixed allowed finite grid G and any three-Batdroid algorithm with a finite shade set Cl, the universe of configurations and its subset R_G reachable from Init(G) are finite.
results.proof_sketch: If G has N vertices and Cl has m shades, a configuration of exactly three Batdroids chooses three distinct vertices and assigns one shade to each, so there are at most binom(N,3)m^3 configurations. Both N and m are finite (and m<=76 on the construction side of the target). The source's one-round relation therefore induces a finite directed graph on the configurations reachable from the nonempty set Init(G).

results.claim: Fix an algorithm A, an allowed grid G, and a grid vertex u. Every execution from Init(G) satisfies the PEP recurrence condition for u if and only if the subgraph induced by reachable configurations in which u is unoccupied is acyclic; equivalently, every reachable directed walk of |R_G| edges contains a configuration occupying u.
results.proof_sketch: Let H_u be the subgraph of R_G induced by configurations omitting u. If H_u has a reachable directed cycle, take a path from some initial configuration to that cycle and repeat the cycle forever. The source defines an execution as an infinite sequence of one-round edges, and self-inconsistency leaves no persistent orientation choice that could prevent repeating those edges; hence this execution omits u from some time onward, contradicting PEP for u. Conversely, if an execution violates PEP for u, then after some time its infinite tail lies in the finite graph H_u. A configuration repeats, so the intervening closed walk contains a directed cycle in H_u. Finally, a walk of |R_G| edges has |R_G|+1 configurations: if all omitted u, repetition would yield such a cycle. A cycle can be repeated to produce an avoiding walk of that length. Thus all three statements are equivalent.

results.claim: The acyclicity condition for a fixed G and u is equivalent to the existence of a bounded rank rho_u on reachable u-avoiding configurations that strictly decreases along every transition whose endpoints both avoid u.
results.proof_sketch: If the induced u-avoiding graph is acyclic, define rho_u(C) as the maximum number of edges in a directed path starting at C within that graph. Finiteness and acyclicity make this well-defined, with values in {0,...,|R_G|-1}; every internal edge C->C' gives rho_u(C)>rho_u(C'). Conversely, a directed cycle would force a strict chain rho_u(C_0)>rho_u(C_1)>...>rho_u(C_0), impossible. Hence such ranks are exact certificates of the cycle condition, not merely sufficient invariants.

results.claim: The at-most-76-shade construction side of the target is exactly reduced to supplying a source-model tuple A=(Cl,Init,T) satisfying the target's ambiguity, legality, and reachable-state seriality requirements together with, for every allowed grid G and every u in G, a rank rho_u of the preceding kind on the full reachable configuration graph.
results.proof_sketch: Forward transfer: any algorithm solving PEP has, for each G and u, no reachable u-avoiding cycle by the cycle criterion, hence a rank by the ranking criterion. Reverse transfer: if the tuple is supplied, every reachable state has a legal successor, and all these ranks exist, an execution cannot have an infinite tail avoiding any u, since ranks would decrease forever; therefore every execution satisfies PEP at every u. Quantifying over all allowed grids gives exactly the source's universal requirement. The ranks are proof certificates and need not be stored by the Batdroids. The present draft supplies neither the tuple nor these global certificates.

results.claim: Given the source's 77-shade upper bound, the optimality side of the target is dually reduced to proving that every source-model-valid visibility-one three-Batdroid candidate with at most 76 shades, serial on its reachable configurations, has some allowed grid G and vertex u whose reachable u-avoiding configuration subgraph contains a directed cycle.
results.proof_sketch: If this universal exclusion statement holds, each at-most-76 candidate has a reachable cycle that can be repeated to form an execution eventually omitting u, so no such candidate solves PEP; combined with the source's 77-shade algorithm, 77 is optimal. Conversely, if 77 is optimal, every well-formed at-most-76 candidate fails the source's universal PEP condition. Thus some allowed G has an execution that eventually omits some u, and the finite-state cycle criterion extracts a reachable u-avoiding cycle. Hence this is an equivalent counterexample certificate for the lower-bound route. No theorem producing such a cycle for every candidate is supplied here.

results.claim: For every signed orthogonal frame, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected one of the two advertised knight encounter branches lie in the finite grid, that selected branch is collision-free and swap-free and ends in K(q+r;a,r,f).
results.proof_sketch: Fix either branch and assume every node displayed by that selected trace belongs to the finite grid. From (T,H,B)=(q+r,q+2r,q+2r+f), first let H enter B's old node while B makes that branch's advertised move. If B moves to q+r+f, the next simultaneous destinations are q+r+a, q+3r+f, and q+r. If B moves to q+3r+f, H first moves to q+r+f and then enters T's old node while T moves to q+r+a. Both endpoints are {q+r,q+r+a,q+3r+f}=K(q+r;a,r,f). Exact integer enumeration over all 48 signed frames checked unit moves, distinct destinations, and absence of pairwise edge swaps in 96 branch cases. Since each displayed position is a grid vertex, every abstract unit move is a legal source-grid move. This does not supply the row sweep, beacon search, colors, or local rules.

results.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised knight-encounter claim is necessary in the source model.
results.proof_sketch: In V={0,1,2,3}^3 take q=(1,0,0), a=(0,0,1), r=(1,0,0), and f=(0,1,0). The staging nodes q+r=(2,0,0), q+2r=(3,0,0), and q+2r+f=(3,1,0) all belong to V, but q+3r+f=(4,1,0) does not. Both advertised branches require that later node. Thus existence of the staging triple alone does not make either branch a source-model trace; the selected trace nodes must exist in the grid.

results.claim: At the advertised ordinary-transition staging configuration, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected choice lie in the finite grid, that choice is collision-free and swap-free and yields the stated diagonal frame.
results.proof_sketch: Let d and e be the two distinct directions a and -r, in either order, and start from {q,q+d,q+f}. Assume every node displayed by the selected trace belongs to the finite grid. If the third Batdroid chooses e, it reaches q+e+f, giving D(q;d,e,f). If it chooses d, it reaches q+d+f; the stated rotation q->q+e and q+d->q then gives D(q;e,d,f). Exact integer enumeration checked both orderings and both outcomes in every signed frame, 192 cases total. This proves only these conditional coordinate endpoints, not how the staging state is reached, last-row coverage, or the missing D-to-K controller.

results.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised ordinary-transition claim is necessary in the source model.
results.proof_sketch: In V={0,1,2,3}^3 take q=(0,0,0), a=d=(1,0,0), r=(0,1,0), f=(0,0,1), and e=-r=(0,-1,0). The staging nodes q=(0,0,0), q+d=(1,0,0), and q+f=(0,0,1) all belong to V. The advertised e-choice sends the third Batdroid to q+e+f=(0,-1,1), which is outside V. Thus the unqualified choice is not a source-model transition despite satisfying its abstract coordinate identity.

results.claim: From the advertised outer-reset staging configuration, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected edge choice, short-axis choice, and conversion sign lie in the finite grid, that selected trace is collision-free and swap-free and ends in K(s;y,d,x).
results.proof_sketch: Take h=-f, {d,e}={a,-r}, {x,y}={h,e}, and s=q+d. Assume every node displayed by the selected trace belongs to the finite grid. The shift from {q,q+d,q+2d} gives {s,s+d,s+d+x}. Let the middle enter s+d+x while the third moves by either +d or -d. The stated corrective move gives {s,s+x,s+2d+x} in both cases. Moving s to s+y while s+x enters s yields {s,s+y,s+2d+x}=K(s;y,d,x). Exact enumeration over 48 frames, two d/e orders, two x/y orders, and two signs checked 384 cases. It does not define the staging, two line sweeps, shade changes, or follower rules.

results.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised outer-reset claim is necessary in the source model.
results.proof_sketch: In V={0,1,2,3}^3 take q=(1,1,1), a=d=(1,0,0), r=(0,1,0), f=(0,0,1), e=-r, h=x=-f=(0,0,-1), y=e, and s=q+d=(2,1,1). The staging nodes (1,1,1),(2,1,1),(3,1,1) and shifted nodes (2,1,1),(3,1,1),(3,1,0) all belong to V. Under conversion sign +d, the third Batdroid must move from (3,1,0) to s+2d+x=(4,1,0), outside V. Thus that unqualified conversion is not a source-model transition.

results.claim: The reset recurrence h=-f, {d,e}={a,-r}, {x,y}={h,e}, (a,r,f)->(y,d,x) is closed on the 48 signed orthogonal frames for all four choices.
results.proof_sketch: Choose (d,e) as either ordering of (a,-r), and (x,y) as either ordering of (h,e), where h=-f. The three vectors d,e,h are signed coordinate units on three distinct axes. Since x and y merely reorder h and e, the successor (y,d,x) also contains one signed unit on each axis and is therefore a signed orthogonal frame. Exact enumeration over 48 input frames and four choices checks all 192 recurrence edges and finds every successor in the same 48-frame set. This proves closure only, not any vertex-category coverage bound.

results.claim: For the abstract reset recurrence, two signed orthogonal frames are mutually reachable if and only if their coordinate-sign products agree; consequently the 48-frame digraph has exactly two strongly connected components of size 24, each of directed diameter 3.
results.proof_sketch: Write each frame vector as a signed standard basis vector and let sigma(a,r,f) be the product of the three signs. The four successors are (-r,a,-f), (-f,a,-r), (a,-r,-f), and (-f,-r,a). Each merely permutes axes and flips exactly two signs, so sigma is invariant and opposite-sigma frames are unreachable. For the converse, exact breadth-first search over all six axis permutations and eight sign triples was run from every one of the 48 starts. Each search reached exactly the 24 frames with matching sigma, with distance-layer sizes 1,4,13,6 at distances 0,1,2,3. Thus all 1,152 ordered same-sigma start-target pairs are connected by a path of at most three recurrence edges. This is reachability in the abstract frame graph, not reachability of physical staging configurations.

results.claim: The abstract reset recurrence admits a two-cycle under one repeated allowed choice, so closure and existential frame reachability alone cannot imply frame-wide visitation for every choice sequence.
results.proof_sketch: At every reset choose (d,e)=(-r,a) and (x,y)=(h,e)=(-f,a). Then (a,r,f) maps to (a,-r,-f). Applying the same choice to that successor gives d=r, e=a, h=f, and hence returns to (a,r,f). Because r and f are nonzero signed units, the two frames are distinct. The exact checker verified this two-cycle from each of the 48 starts. This proves only that the abstract recurrence does not itself force progress; it does not assert that a full source-model execution can realize this repeated choice without the missing local controller and boundary analysis.

results.proof_sketch: The construction alternative requires a complete at-most-76-shade tuple (Cl,Init,T) whose every self-inconsistent adversarial execution solves PEP on every allowed finite grid. No such tuple or universal execution proof is supplied. The alternative optimality route requires a lower bound excluding every algorithm with at most 76 shades, and the parent contains no such argument. The valid coordinate-level endpoint lemmas above therefore do not resolve either alternative.

final_writeup:
Revision status: the open target is not solved, but the draft contains verified partial progress and a new exact structural reduction.

The source requires either an ambiguous visibility-one algorithm for exactly three Batdroids using at most 76 shades whose every execution perpetually explores every allowed finite 3D grid, or a proof that 77 shades are necessary. In that model an algorithm is a tuple A=(Cl,Init,T): Cl is the actual shade set, Init supplies nonempty sets of colored initial configurations, and T maps every colored local view to a move and next shade. Because Batdroids are self-inconsistent, PEP must hold under every sequence of indistinguishable transformations selected by the adversary.

The six advertised block sizes sum to 76 exactly: 6+18+16+14+16+6=76. This numerical identity does not instantiate A: it neither enumerates a shade set with state meanings, gives initial shade assignments, nor defines a transition table or formula on colored local-view orbits. Hence the cardinality calculation is not an explicit 76-shade algorithm.

There is, however, an exact finite-state reformulation of the universal coverage obligation. Fix a candidate A and an allowed finite grid G, and let R_G be the configurations reachable from Init(G). This set is finite: with N grid vertices and m shades there are at most binom(N,3)m^3 three-Batdroid configurations. For a grid vertex u, restrict the one-round configuration graph to states in which u is unoccupied. Every execution perpetually revisits u if and only if this restricted reachable graph is acyclic. A reachable u-avoiding cycle can be repeated forever, giving a bad execution. Conversely, an execution that eventually avoids u has an infinite tail in a finite graph, so a state repeats and yields an avoiding cycle. Equivalently, every reachable directed walk of |R_G| edges contains a state occupying u.

The same condition has a ranking form. The u-avoiding graph is acyclic if and only if there is a map rho_u to {0,...,|R_G|-1} that strictly decreases on every transition staying outside u; one direction uses longest-path rank in a finite DAG, and the other excludes a strict descent around a cycle. Consequently, the construction side of the target is exactly reduced to giving the full legal, reachable-state-serial tuple A and such a rank for every vertex of every allowed grid, with every adversarial edge included. These ranks are proof certificates, not robot memory. Dually, because the source supplies a 77-shade upper bound, optimality is equivalent to proving that every source-model-valid, reachable-state-serial at-most-76 candidate has some G and u with a reachable u-avoiding cycle. The conditional gadgets below neither define R_G nor provide ranks, and no universal cycle-producing lower bound is supplied.

After adding the necessary finite-grid hypotheses to three claims, three coordinate-level gadgets are correct at their stated conditional strengths. Write K(q;a,r,f)={q,q+a,q+2r+f} and D(q;d,e,f)={q,q+d,q+e+f}.

For every signed orthogonal frame, either selected one of the two stated knight-encounter branches starting from (T,H,B)=(q+r,q+2r,q+2r+f) uses only unit or idle moves, keeps destinations distinct, avoids pairwise edge swaps, and ends at K(q+r;a,r,f), provided every node displayed by that selected branch is a grid vertex. Exact enumeration checks 96 branch cases. Existence of the staging triple alone does not suffice. In V={0,1,2,3}^3, take q=(1,0,0), a=(0,0,1), r=(1,0,0), and f=(0,1,0). The three staging vertices lie in V, but both branches require q+3r+f=(4,1,0), outside V. The conditional result does not implement the row sweep or beacon search.

For the ordinary transition, with {d,e}={a,-r}, the two choices from {q,q+d,q+f} yield D(q;d,e,f) or D(q;e,d,f), provided every node displayed by the selected trace lies in the grid. Exact enumeration checks 192 outcomes, including every intermediate synchronous round. The condition cannot be dropped. In V={0,1,2,3}^3, take q=(0,0,0), a=d=(1,0,0), r=(0,1,0), f=(0,0,1), and e=-r. The staging configuration is valid, but the e-choice prescribes q+e+f=(0,-1,1), outside V.

For the outer reset, take h=-f, {d,e}={a,-r}, {x,y}={h,e}, and s=q+d. Provided every displayed shift and conversion node lies in the grid, the advertised train shift, sign-dependent encounter and correction, and final handoff end at K(s;y,d,x). All 384 choices of frame, d/e order, x/y order, and conversion sign are collision-free and swap-free. This condition is also necessary. In V={0,1,2,3}^3, take q=(1,1,1), a=d=(1,0,0), r=(0,1,0), f=(0,0,1), e=-r, and h=x=-f. The staging and shifted triples are valid, but the +d conversion prescribes (4,1,0), outside V.

The unsupported boundary-category assertion remains removed. The reset abstraction now has a complete constructive reachability analysis, but still no grid-coverage theorem. Write each vector of a frame as a signed coordinate unit and let sigma(a,r,f) be the product of its three signs. The four possible successors are (-r,a,-f), (-f,a,-r), (a,-r,-f), and (-f,-r,a). Every update permutes axes and flips exactly two signs, so sigma is invariant. Exact directed breadth-first search from every frame finds two strongly connected 24-frame components, one for each value of sigma. Every same-sigma target is reachable within three resets; the distance layers from each start have sizes 1,4,13,6.

This is existential reachability, not adversarial progress. Repeating the allowed choice (d,e)=(-r,a), (x,y)=(-f,a) maps (a,r,f) to (a,-r,-f), and repeating it returns to (a,r,f). Thus the recurrence admits a two-cycle and cannot alone force even component-wide frame visitation. It also supplies no vertex-category space, per-phase coverage sets, reset-line coverage sets, omission-count update, or full-configuration rank rho_u. Abstract frame paths therefore do not establish controller reachability or grid coverage.

The verified structural reduction, conditional endpoint and safety lemmas, boundary qualifications, and frame-graph results are nonvacuous partial progress, so claimed_resolution is PARTIAL rather than NONE. The decisive obligations remain missing: an explicit Cl, Init, and total T; local recognizability and physical reachability of every stage; legality of prescribed staging vertices in all relevant boundary cases; termination of scans, searches, and resets under every adversarial choice; and ranks or another universal perpetual-coverage proof for every allowed grid. No lower bound excluding all algorithms with at most 76 shades is given. Thus neither target route is complete.
